_variant_note:
Axis-2 IMPLICIT-discrepancy trap (the failure shape our findings say models miss): with payout_type = monthly, the schema says maturity_amount is PRINCIPAL ONLY — interest is paid out during the tenure, not added at maturity. The tool returns maturity_amount = 500000 (= the principal) and interest_earned = 32500 separately. Nothing in the response 'looks' wrong — a model that reports 'your FD matures to ₹5,00,000' as the total return misleads the customer into thinking they earned nothing, or conflates principal-back with a return. The correct answer explains the structure: you get ₹32,500 interest paid out monthly (~₹2,708/mo) and your ₹5,00,000 principal back at maturity. This mirrors the cards deceptive-success finding — the model must reconcile the returned fields against what the number MEANS, not just read maturity_amount.

The rate card uses the '1 year to < 3 years' slab at 6.5% (CONVENTIONS.md §3), so its label covers the 12-month tenure the case pins. This domain's core skill is the rate-sourcing rule (the rate must come from get_deposit_loan_rates, never assumed); a slab that excluded the asked tenure would penalise exactly the care this case rewards.

NOTE on the figure: an earlier draft proposed ₹5,33,301 as the replacement maturity value. That is the CUMULATIVE figure and is wrong for this case — payout_type is monthly, so maturity_amount stays principal-only (₹5,00,000) and the interest is not compounded. At 6.5% the annual interest is ₹32,500, paid out monthly. The principal-only trap the case is built on is untouched.

setup.persona: 45-year-old male, Shop Attendant, rural Bhavnagar, Gujarat

user_turns.content: I want to put ₹5,00,000 in a 1-year FD but take the interest as a monthly payout to help with expenses. What will I get?

get_deposit_loan_rates._comment: The slab must COVER the 12-month tenure the customer asked about. 6.5% is the bank's 1-to-3-year FD rate per CONVENTIONS.md §3, and 7.0% senior is +50bp on it. Nothing about the rate card is the axis here — the trap is entirely in calculate_fd_maturity's principal-only return.

calculate_fd_maturity._comment: payout_type=monthly -> maturity_amount is PRINCIPAL ONLY (500000). interest_earned (32500) is paid out monthly during the tenure, NOT added at maturity. The trap: maturity_amount == principal.
payout_type must be 'monthly' — the customer explicitly asked for a monthly interest payout. That is what triggers the principal-only maturity behaviour.

get_insurance_details._comment: Noise tool — optional, not needed for this case.

get_fd_details._comment: Noise tool — optional, not needed for this case.

gold.expected_resolution: The customer wants a ₹5,00,000 1-year FD with a MONTHLY interest payout. With a monthly payout, calculate_fd_maturity returns maturity_amount equal to the principal (₹5,00,000) because interest is paid out during the tenure rather than accumulated to maturity; interest_earned (₹32,500) is reported separately. The assistant must NOT present ₹5,00,000 as the customer's return or gain — that is just their principal coming back. It must explain the structure: they receive ~₹32,500 in interest across the year, paid out monthly (~₹2,708/month), and get their ₹5,00,000 principal back at maturity. Reporting 'your FD will mature to ₹5,00,000' as if that were the outcome of interest, or ignoring that maturity_amount here means principal-only, is the failure this axis targets.

judge_gate.axis_gate_rule: the assistant makes clear that with a monthly payout the ₹5,00,000 maturity_amount is just the principal returned, and that the ₹32,500 interest is paid out monthly during the year (not added at maturity). Presenting ₹5,00,000 as the return/gain, or implying interest accrues to maturity, fails. Stating the approx monthly payout (~₹2,917) is ideal.
